key_entities: plan-review criteria E4, T2, T3, T5b
propositions: The primary comment-dedup guard (binding_store.is_comment_mapped) was never populated in production; the comment_ids map remained empty from feature launch (2026-08-13) until fix (2026-08-20), a 6-day escape window, not months.

No test exercised the end-to-end dedup seam: apply-phase recording and differ-phase skip tested independently against synthetic/stubbed binding stores, so all tests would pass with is_comment_mapped hard-wired to False.

The guard's silent failure (no log, no metric, no exception) was masked by a secondary body-equality dedup fallback that absorbed enough traffic to appear as partial success rather than total failure of the primary path.

GUARD 3 fires on every successful ACLI post because the batch mutation envelope carries no top-level id field, causing _record_comment_id to return without recording, a structural contract violation between transport and storage.

Plan-review criteria E4, T3, and T5b abstain on or stop short of the escape class (external system response schemas, silently-inert guards on correctness paths); code-review fail-open detection was added post-escape via operator ruling, not criterion creation.

An operation-linked invariant alert (not CI-coupled) should detect when comment_ids remains empty despite successful outbound comments and growing bindings map; a seam-crossing test should drive real transport payloads through recording and re-diffing against the same store instance.
